extracted.intended_audience: chemical indexers, patent searchers, and patent information specialists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assigning and searching chemical functional-group codes in patent documents (coding rules, negation codes, tautomer handling, attachment priorities, and search-strategy construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer most-specific codes; avoid redundant less-specific codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes occurring later in a Part or Set are often less specific, or cover fewer atoms, than the first applicable code(s). Even though these less-specific codes may also appear to be applicable to the functional group, they are not used if they add no new information about the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add a less-specific code if it provides no additional structural information (example: a structure coded Y-C(=T)-X (L511) should not be further coded as -C(=T)-X (L512); a compound coded -O-S-N (K340) should not be further coded as Y-S-N (K352)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to add codes for variable element symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: If the definition of an applicable code includes variable element symbols (T, U, V, W, X, Y and/or Z), additional codes are used to identify the elements represented by the symbols, unless the first code states that this should not be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a functional group represented by single code L410 may still require K820 and L463 to identify elements represented by T, U, and Y. Note exceptions such as 'no additional codes should be used to identify the “T” atom in functional groups searched with the code L620' (see note on page 162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Parts H: and J: when K: and L: do not fully define functional groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If all functional groups in a structure have not been fully defined by codes from Parts K: and L:, Parts H: and J: can be scanned for relevant codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts H: and J: include common functional groups (amine, hydroxy, mercapto, ether, thioether, halogen, C=C, C#C, carboxylic acid, thiocarboxylic acid, ester, thioester, amide, thioamide, aldehyde, thioaldehyde, oxo, and thioxo). These groups may nonetheless be coded in K: or L: depending on bonded atoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautomerism: keto-enol / thioxo-thiol rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When keto-enol (thioxo-thiol) tautomerism is possible, the structure is searched in the keto (thioxo) form, unless the -OH (-SH) group of the enol (thiol) form is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring, e.g. benzene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided show specific code selections (e.g., search as J521 'Oxo bonded to heterocyclic C', NOT H421 '-OH bonded to heterocyclic C' when tautomerism applies). Hydroxy bonded to fully conjugated carbocycle is treated as enol and may be coded H443 rather than the keto-related J563.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imine tautomerization rule for ring C
rubrics_metrics.description: An imine group (>C=N-) in which the C atom is part of a ring is tautomerized and searched in the =C-NH- form if such tautomerization causes the N atom to form an amine or amide group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tautomerization leads to an N group other than amine or amide, the imine form is coded. Example: code H121 ('1 amine bonded to a heterocycle') is used NOT L355 ('C=N') when tautomerization creates an amine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation codes (essential codes): assignment principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A negation code is assigned by coders when the functional group represented by that code is present in ALL variations of a disclosed compound in a patent document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negation codes denote groups 'essential' to the disclosed compounds and are intended to allow users to remove records that exclusively disclose those essential groups (i.e., to eliminate false drops) without removing records that also disclose compounds of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: User use of negation codes (LINK NOT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Negation codes are searched negatively by users using the operator LINK NOT to eliminate irrelevant answers that only disclose unwanted essential groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only negate a negation code when it is known with certainty that the corresponding functional group is not present in any variation of the structures being searched. If there is any possibility the group may be present in variable/undefined R groups, do not negate the negation code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not negate four-character chemical codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The four-character chemical codes (e.g. H441 'One aromatic hydroxy') should not be negated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemical codes in a single code subfield often represent many different possible structures; negating a four-character chemical code could eliminate records that include both unwanted and wanted compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: K0 usage for absence of K: and L: groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If a search structure contains none of the functional groups defined in Parts K: and L:, the negation code K0 can be negated in place of all of the individual K: and L: negation codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K0 provides a shorthand to negate all K: and L: negation codes when none of those groups are relevant to the search structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other available negation codes and typical placement in search
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside of Parts H:, J:, K:, and L:, available negation codes include M1 (ring linkage) and V0 (natural products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negation codes are not linked to particular time ranges, but are usually negated at the end of the search strategy to remove false drops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation-code search-strategy principle (do not lose relevant records)
rubrics_metrics.description: When formulating a search strategy, do not negate any functional group that could conceivably be present in the structure being searched so that no relevant references are lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a structure's R groups can be halogen, NO2, or OCH3, these variable groups are not 'essential' and therefore should not be negated; instead negate all negation codes EXCEPT those corresponding to essential groups known to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: H/J codes are hierarchical (digit meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most codes in Parts H: and J: are hierarchical: the first digit indicates the type of functional group represented; the second digit indicates the type of group to which the functional group is bonded (the 'attachment group'); and the third digit indicates the number of times a particular functional group/attachment group combination is present in a structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hierarchy informs code selection and truncation strategies when unknown substituents are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thio-analogues coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Thiocarboxylic acids, thioxo groups, and thioethers have their own codes; they do not receive the codes of their oxygen analogues. Other thio functional groups receive the codes of their corresponding oxygen analogues, as well as a general code indicating that these codes are being used for the thio analogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a single thiocarboxylic acid group bonded to a heterocyclic ring is coded J191. A thiocarboxylic ester bonded via thionyl to a heterocyclic ring gets J211 ('One ester or thioester ...') plus J290 ('Thioester').

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional groups bonded to Z atoms exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functional groups that normally receive codes from Part H: or Part J: do not receive those codes when they are bonded to B, Si, P, or As ('Z' atoms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for coding functional groups bonded to Z atoms are given in the Notes pertaining to Part B: codes (see page 47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment-group taxonomy and coding consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four types of attachment groups that are coded: (a) Heterocyclic ring, (b) Aromatic ring, (c) Alicyclic ring, (d) Aliphatic chain. In most cases, the atom of attachment must be C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nitro groups are special and may be searched using codes in Set H3: when bonded to either a C atom or an N atom of the attachment group. Use the attachment-group digit (second digit) when selecting H/J codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority order for multivalent functional-group coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes of multivalent functional groups (amines, ethers, esters, amides, and sulphur analogues) are chosen according to the attachment group with the highest priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority order used: Heterocyclic ring > Aromatic ring > Alicyclic ring > Aliphatic chain. Example: compound coded H541 ('One aromatic ether'), but not H561 ('1 alicyclic ether').

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-symmetrical multivalent groups: point-of-attachment priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-symmetrical, multivalent functional groups are additionally coded according to the point of attachment of the highest priority group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an amide bonded to an aliphatic C on the carbonyl side and to a heterocyclic C on the N side is coded J321 ('One amide group bonded to a heterocyclic ring via N'). If attachment groups on both sides are equal priority, the code for the carbonyl (or thionyl) attachment has higher priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fused rings do not change the ring-attachment coding
rubrics_metrics.description: The codes in many Sets in Parts H: and J: refer to monovalent functional groups bonded to heterocyclic, aromatic, and alicyclic rings; only the ring to which the functional group is bonded is taken into consideration—the presence of further rings fused to the substituted ring has no effect on the choice of an applicable code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an amine bonded to an aromatic ring fused to a heterocyclic ring is coded H141 ('One amine bonded to an aromatic C atom'), not codes reflecting the fused presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Se/Te coding: get S-analogues plus Part B:
rubrics_metrics.description: A compound with an Se or Te atom receives all codes from Parts H: and J: that would be applicable if Se or Te were replaced by S. In addition, Se and Te atoms are themselves coded in Part B:.

rubrics_metrics.name: C atom in multiple rings: choose highest-priority ring (with bridged exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the C atom to which a functional group is bonded is a member of more than one ring, the highest priority ring (heterocyclic > aromatic > alicyclic > aliphatic) determines which functional group code is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the atom bonded to the functional group is a non-angular C atom in a bridged ring system, and if the C atom could be seen as being a member of different sized rings, the smallest ring size is chosen even if it is of lower priority than the larger ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy with variable/unknown substituents: OR applicable codes
rubrics_metrics.description: If known functional groups are present in a structure that also has unknown structural fragments (R groups), each known functional group is considered separately, and the codes that would be applicable to that functional group for all definitions of R are OR'ed together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broadens the search to include all possible applicable codes for the known piece while avoiding omission of relevant records. Use truncated Subset codes (e.g., H12: OR H14: OR ...) when any number of such groups may be present in undefined portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truncation of subset codes to allow variable multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: When R or R' may contain additional groups of the same type, use truncated Subset codes (e.g., H12: OR H14: OR H16:) to indicate any number of amino groups bonded to any attachment group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truncated subset codes indicate unknown multiplicity or occurrence count in undefined portions of the structure; used in Examples 3–6 for amines, oxo groups, esters, and ethers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amines definition for coding
rubrics_metrics.description: An amine is defined as a trivalent N atom that is (1) single-bonded to three atoms, all of which are C or H, at least one of which is C; (2) not bonded to any C atom that is multiply bonded to a heteroatom, unless the C atom and the heteroatom are part of the same ring system; (3) if N is a ring member, all three atoms of attachment are C, and the three C atoms are not members of the same ring system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliphatic amines are coded in Set H1:, amines in which N is a ring member are coded in Set H2:. N atoms that do not meet these criteria are 'non-amines' and are coded elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring tertiary nitrogen coding and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring tertiary nitrogen is a trivalent N atom in a ring, bonded to an atom other than H that is outside the N atom’s ring system. Ring tertiary nitrogens may be either amines or non-amines, and are coded in Set H2:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ring tertiary amines additionally receive a code from Set H1: based on the C group bonded from outside the ring (e.g., H202 with H141/H181 combos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydroxy/mercapto coding and tautomer considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keto-enol (thioxo-thiol) tautomerism can significantly affect coding of hydroxy groups: structures are coded in keto form unless the -OH (-SH) of the enol (thiol) is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some classes (hemi-acetals, hemi-thioacetals, non-cyclic hemi-ketals, hemi-thioketals, aldehyde hydrates) are not searchable in H4: and are coded elsewhere (e.g., L6:, J471/J490). Use H40/H42/H44/H46/H48 subset codes per count and attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halogen coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set H6: codes are assigned to every monovalent halogen atom bonded to a C atom that is not doubly bonded to O or S. Subset H60: is used to identify X atoms in functional groups coded L330 and L353.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To retrieve all disclosures of specific halogens use (H601 OR H602 OR H603 OR H604 OR H685). To retrieve specific and non-specific disclosures add H600, but H600 should never be searched without at least one specific-halogen code. H607 applies to per-halo compounds with only -C(=W)-H C-H bonds. H608/H609 denote multiple occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olefin/acetylinic coding rules and conjugation counting
rubrics_metrics.description: H7 codes identify >C=C< and -C#C- groups; exocyclic >C=C< (H720) vs internal and counts of conjugated/unconjugated double bonds (H721-H725) are distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugation does not include double bonds in rings, but conjugation continues through one single bond in a ring. Exocyclic >C=C< groups are not counted when applying H721-H723. Some H71 codes (e.g., H711, H712, H724) can be assigned to groups with more than one atom in the same ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part J: symbol definitions and coding scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In Part J: definitions, symbols are defined: T = O,S,Se,Te (valency II); T' = S,Se,Te (valency IV or more); U = O,S,Se,Te,or N; R = C or H; X = halogen; Y = O,S,Se,Te,N,or halogen. To be coded in Part J: the carbonyl (or thionyl) side of the functional group must be directly bonded to H or C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: oxo and thioxo groups bonded to ring C atoms are coded in Set J5: even if further bonded solely to O, S, Se, Te, N, or halogen. Some groups (listed) are NOT coded in Part J: but in L4, L5, L520, etc.; conversely some groups ARE coded in Part J: (table of examples).
